issue: 'balasan pesan dari dia' stacks two nouns awkwardly — natives say 'balasan darinya' or 'balasan pesannya', not 'a reply-of-message from him'; 'dari dia' after formal 'sedang menunggu' also mixes registers.

fix.english: I am waiting for a reply from him.

issue: 'berjanji datang' clips the complement — a promise about a future act takes 'akan': 'berjanji akan datang'. Bare 'berjanji datang' reads as truncated textbook prose.

fix.target: Dia berjanji akan datang, tapi tidak muncul.
fix.english: He promised he would come, but did not show up.

issue: 'Telepon dari kantor itu' parses most naturally as 'the call from that office', and the present-tense gloss is odd for a phone call. Natives anchor it in time: 'telepon dari kantor tadi'.

fix.target: Telepon dari kantor tadi penting sekali.
fix.english: That call from the office earlier was very important.

issue: Register: 'ponsel' is the written-media word — across a table everyone says 'HP' (ha-pe). 'meminjam telepon teman' doubles down with dated 'telepon' for a handset. Q2 should model the spoken word.

fix.target: HP saya mati, jadi saya pinjam HP teman.
fix.english: My phone died, so I borrowed a friend's phone.
fix.grammar: HP (say: ha-pe) is the spoken word for phone: HP saya mati = my phone died.

issue: Register clash: formal 'bertemu' inside a casual meetup arrangement closed with 'ya'. When fixing a meeting spot with a friend, the universal spoken verb is 'ketemu'.

fix.target: Kita ketemu di depan pintu masuk mal, ya.
fix.english: We will meet in front of the mall entrance, okay.
fix.grammar: ketemu is the spoken form of bertemu: kita ketemu jam lima = we meet at five.

issue: Gloss mismatch: 'tidak menyala' = 'is not on' (a state), but the gloss says 'does not turn on'. For a light that refuses to come on, natives say 'tidak mau menyala' or just 'mati'.

fix.target: Lampu di kamar mandi tidak mau menyala.
fix.english: The light in the bathroom will not turn on.
fix.grammar: tidak mau + verb for things = won't: lampunya tidak mau menyala = it won't turn on.

issue: 'hilang satu' is countable-English phrasing — for one of a pair (socks, shoes, gloves) the idiom is 'hilang sebelah'.

fix.target: Kaus kaki saya hilang sebelah di kamar.
fix.english: One of my socks is missing in the room.
fix.grammar: sebelah = one of a pair: hilang sebelah = one of the two is missing.

issue: 'mengecat pagar dengan warna hijau' is wordy report-style phrasing ('with the color green'); spoken Indonesian attaches the color directly: 'mengecat pagar warna hijau' or 'mengecat pagar hijau'.

fix.target: Ayah sedang mengecat pagar warna hijau.
fix.english: Dad is painting the fence green.

issue: Calque of 'bed sheets': 'seprai tempat tidur' is redundant — 'seprai' already means bed sheet and never takes 'tempat tidur' after it.

fix.english: She changes the sheets every week.

issue: 'terlihat bagus untuk kamu' is a word-for-word calque of 'looks good on/for you'. The Indonesian idiom for clothes suiting someone is 'cocok' (or colloquially 'bagus di kamu').

fix.target: Rok merah itu cocok sekali untuk kamu.
fix.english: That red skirt really suits you.

issue: 'Kemarin kami tiba ... malam hari' is a roundabout calque of 'Yesterday we arrived at night' — the natural time phrase is simply 'kemarin malam' (last night).

fix.target: Kami tiba di Jakarta kemarin malam.
fix.english: We arrived in Jakarta last night.

issue: 'di mana tempat terbaik?' calques 'where is the best place?' — 'terbaik' is written register, and natives ask 'di mana yang paling bagus?' instead of naming an abstract 'tempat'.

fix.target: Kalau mau tukar uang, di mana yang paling bagus?
fix.english: If I want to exchange money, where is the best place?

issue: Gloss fidelity: bare 'rekan' reads as 'associate/partner', not 'colleague' — the everyday office word is 'rekan kerja'.

fix.target: Saya butuh rekan kerja yang bisa bantu proyek ini.
fix.english: I need a colleague who can help with this project.

issue: 'saya kabari kamu segera' puts 'segera' in English sentence-final adverb position; natives front it onto the verb: 'saya langsung kabari kamu' / 'segera saya kabari'.

fix.target: Kalau rapat batal, saya langsung kabari kamu.
fix.english: If the meeting is cancelled, I'll let you know right away.
fix.grammar: -i makes a verb aim at someone: kabar (news) → kabari = let (someone) know.

issue: Collocation: emails are 'dibalas', not 'dijawab' — 'balas email' is the fixed pairing (cf. membalas for replying to messages); 'jawab email' is English 'answer emails' leaking through.

fix.target: Sebelum pulang, saya harus balas tiga email lagi.
fix.english: Before going home, I have to reply to three more emails.

issue: 'bantu ... dengan tugas sekolahnya' is the English 'help with X' calque — 'membantu dengan' is not an Indonesian pattern; help + the action: 'bantu adik mengerjakan tugasnya'.

fix.target: Tolong bantu adik kamu mengerjakan tugas sekolahnya.
fix.english: Please help your little brother do his schoolwork.
